name: Apex Predator
title: Apex Predator
sections: Becomes Enraged and Dangerous when grabbed or hurt
The Apex Predator, commonly known as the Duck, is a Level 1 Monster in R.E.P.O. and acts as a seemingly innocent creature until the player tries to touch it.
1 Appearance
The Apex Predator resembles a small duckling with wide adorable eyes and a round cute body. It stays this way until it is pet.
Once pet it becomes enraged. It retains the general shape but it flies with a comically wide beak with horrific sharp teeth. The cute eyes are barely visible in the enraged form.

Upon spotting a player, the Apex Predator will follow them, constantly trying to stay on their crosshair position to bait the player to grab it. If the player looks up or jumps, the duck will jump as well to maintain visibility.

If grabbed or damaged by anything, the Apex Predator will become enraged and grow a large, toothy maw before immediately chasing the player who angered it (or the closest player if damaged indirectly). It will be aggressive for ten seconds and begin rapidly biting, dealing damage up to three times per second. It can follow players underneath or above objects, such as tables. Once it begins its pursuit, it will always know the location of the player it's targeting. Hiding is impossible, so outrunning it is the only option.
If the Apex Predator falls into a pit, it will fly back up unless stunned. It can continuously fly for 30 seconds, and will exhaust itself and fall to its death after the 30 seconds are up.

Luring the Apex Predator into a toilet (and flushing) or a Swiftbroom cauldron will launch and stun it for ~14 seconds. It can be slammed to death while stunned.
Note that the Museum does have security lasers, but these are not necessarily assured to kill it. They do not keep it stunned for very long or do enough damage for it to be a feasible tech.
Note that the Museum does have security lasers, but these are not necessarily assured to kill it. They do not keep it stunned for very long or do enough damage for it to be a feasible tech.

It’s possible to stun the Apex Predator by tumble launching into it, dealing 15 damage. It will usually get pushed back far and fast, usually taking additional Physics damage. However, this is difficult to pull off due to its small size and airborne movement.
It will become aggressive to the closest player within 10 units around it. If no players are around that area, it will get back up and do nothing.

The Apex Predator can be crushed by an extraction point for an easy kill. It will remain largely stationary at the location of the players cursor. This, conveniently, also gives the player the money from its Enemy Valuable if the duck is far enough into extraction. But if it is too close to the edge, the valuable will remain as an item instead of being sold and can be sold at the next extraction.

The Apex Predator loses interest quickly. Running into the next room and hiding under something is often enough for it to stop pursuing the player.  
However, since the Apex Predator follows the player's cursor, looking at a wall with an adjacent room behind it to guide it into that room and break line of sight. After a few seconds, it will lose track of the player.

However, since the Apex Predator follows the player's cursor, looking at a wall with an adjacent room behind it to guide it into that room and break line of sight. After a few seconds, it will lose track of the player.
Since the Apex Predator cannot fly forever, players can attempt to push it into a pit then block it above with any big item, like a C.A.R.T., until it falls.

Even in its enraged state, the Apex Predator can still be stunned and/or killed. A carefully aimed attack will disrupt its aggression, although it will enrage again once it recovers from the stun unless killed.

It is impossible to lift the duck, as the player would require 833,328 Strength Upgrades to achieve 999,999 force required. Even debug editing, the maximum is less than 100, preventing this from being achievable.
With mods, it is possible to lift the duck; if done, the player will get the same result as when they pick up any other monster, except that it will stay docile.

A painting in the Museum of Human Art shows what appears to be Dumgolf using his staff on a duck, implying that the duck's mutations are a byproduct of a spell.
Another painting in the Museum depicts the Apex Predator in Cubism, implying that monsters were known about prior to the Incident that left the world in the current state.
The Apex Predator's damage per second is the same as Reaper's being 10 damage every ~0.2 seconds.

name: Gnome
title: Gnome
sections: The Gnome is a Level 1 Monster in R.E.P.O.. It acts as a mischievous creature that looks to damage semibots and valuables.
1 Appearance

Gnomes are small, devilish mobs, resembling a miniature animate garden gnome with a distorted face. They wear a red cap, blue tunic, brown belt and boots. They have a full, white beard and mustache. Their mouth is open showing a set of sharp teeth. Their eyes are fully black and their noise is pointed.

Gnomes always spawn in groups of four unless replacing a level 3 Monster. When roaming, they will stop at random spots while remaining grouped with the other Gnomes in the level. When a Gnome detects a valid Valuable or a player nearby, it will alert other Gnomes nearby and attempt to attack said valuable/player by swinging a pickaxe at it. Gnomes prioritize Valuables over players.

Gnomes can jump and enter the cart which can easily cause a lot of items getting damaged from one swing. They can also jump onto tables or similar objects if there is a player on top, and jump when a player jumps if trying to attack.

They can be picked up with no strength, making them easy to kill by simply smashing them against something or throwing in the air. You can pick one up as a weapon to smash against or drop on his fellow Gnome folk, killing both on impact.
If the valuable they want to damage is being held above a pit they will jump into said pit.
If swarmed by a lot of gnomes, repeatedly jumping will make it more difficult for them to land hits.
When they are lurking they can easily find you on the ground level. Hide higher up, in a chest, a cabinet, or a closable hiding place.

Because monsters have a one-second respawn timer after the last extraction is completed, Gnomes may respawn in overwhelming numbers in later levels. It is better to just try and run from them rather than fight.
There is a small chance that a level 3 monster that would have spawned will be replaced by 10 gnomes.

If you have another semibot nearby, you can keep the valuable the gnomes are targeting suspended in midair to pacify them while the other semibot grabs and chucks them away one by one, reducing their potential to damage and injure.
If they attack a Camera (or a cart that contains one) it will flash and instantly destroy them.

The Pulse Pistol can eradicate an entire group of gnomes in one shot if timed and aimed correctly. Combined with its decent ammo supply, this makes it one of the better methods to get rid of gnomes quickly and cleanly where needed.
Because the Boltzap's projectile has a very small blast radius, it also works as effectively if the gnomes are grouped up, since its low damage output is still potentially enough to kill the gnomes if they take impact damage after the hit.

Because the Boltzap's projectile has a very small blast radius, it also works as effectively if the gnomes are grouped up, since its low damage output is still potentially enough to kill the gnomes if they take impact damage after the hit.
The Gnome is one of only two monsters that has a weight of Very Light (0) along with the Banger.
The sounds for the Gnome are taken from the Minions in Despicable Me.

name: Chef
title: Chef
sections: The Chef, often called the Frog, is a Level 2 Monster in R.E.P.O. that attacks by tumbling with its 2 small cleavers.
1 Appearance
The Chef is a green, clumsy, Relatively Small Creature that resembles a Frog wearing a bloody chefs uniform.

Starting with the Chefs head, it wears a chefs hat, lightly covered in blood, Its eyes are black with horizontal yellow pupils, the Chefs mouth has drips of blood on it, and above its mouth is a small, black, mustache.
On the Chefs torso, it wears its sleeved uniform, which is mostly covered in blood. It has 2 arms and legs, with 4 fingers including the thumb.

In the Chefs attack animations, it opens its mouth revealing its teeth and gums. It has 9 sharp teeth with 5 on the top row, and 4 on the bottom row. It spawns in 2 Cleavers during its attack animation. These cleavers are metallic and have blood on it and are the Chefs main weapon.
The Chef will be aimlessly frog hopping around the level until it spots a semibot.

Once the Chef spots a semibot, it will make a noise, hop up to them, and when close enough to the semibot, the Chef will start its attack. It stands still and it has a large delay, the attack is indicated by the Chef smiling and then pulling out its cleavers. It will turn itself at the direction of the targeted semibot until the delay has ended.

After the Chef's delay, it will start tumbling and lunge itself at a very fast speed to whatever direction it was looking at (dependent on where the semibot was), slightly bouncing up and swinging its cleavers. The Chef also turns into a Physics object while attacking, which means it will bounce around, can be picked up, etc. The Chef will deal 10 damage every time it hits a semibot or monster, it will also stun them and smaller monsters for a short time.
The Chef can be a very serious threat to valuables as it can damage them, especially to valuables that are fragile, have higher value, or both.

After some time, the Chef will stop attacking and either go back to roaming, or leave, where it will mostly ignore the semibots, usually indicated when the Chef turns around after reaching the place it wanted to go to.
A painting in the Museum of Human Art depicts a Chef attacking a person, suggesting at least a fear of Chefs by humans if not that Chefs commonly attack them.
If a player crouches right after the Chef starts tumbling, it can fly over that players head.

Players can use the Chef can be used to help them as it will lunge forward to wherever the targeted player was when tumbling, they can use this to your advantage by baiting him into damaging another monster, players can also do this with pits for an easy kill, or with other players if they want to troll them.

If a player is being targeted by the Chef, after it starts tumbling, another player can grab the Chef, usually preventing it from going anywhere and saving the player being targeted by the Chef.
The Chef will not be stunned if grabbed in this way, even if grabbed in mid-air, nor can it be slammed. It will also continue flailing its cleavers around, doing damage to anything close enough. Players will have to stun it manually before it can be slammed as usual.

The Chef will not be stunned if grabbed in this way, even if grabbed in mid-air, nor can it be slammed. It will also continue flailing its cleavers around, doing damage to anything close enough. Players will have to stun it manually before it can be slammed as usual.

Players should avoid getting cornered by the Chef. That's when it's most dangerous. It can stun them and fall on top of a player while still flailing, inflicting serious damage. If cornered, players can dash and jump past it again while it's preparing to attack. Tumbling into the Chef directly is a dangerous trick for players but they can stun it for a second at the cost of some health which grants Players more of an opening to escape.

The Chef is prone to ricocheting off of furniture such as chairs while trying to attack a player underneath it. If spotted, they  can try to hide underneath something with a very low roof, and hide as far back under it as they possibly can. If the chef tries to attack, it will likely bounce off the object and miss completely before losing sight of the targeted player again.
Players can launch into Chef Frog until it is dead, as it will stun it, though it takes away 20 hp.
In the game files, the Chef is known as "Tumbler".

name: Elsa
title: Elsa
sections: Becomes enraged when not grabbed or gets hurt
Elsa is a Level 1 Monster in R.E.P.O. and was added in V0.3.0 (The Monster Update), it acts as an attention-seeking creature that wants some pets from the semibots.
1 Appearance

4 History

4.1 V0.3.0
4.2 V0.3.1.2 beta
7 References

Elsa appears as a small, white puppy, with no special unique features. Elsa's expression is always a wide open smile, unless it is stunned in which case she has a frown.  As Elsa starts getting more agitated, her eyes start to shift from black to red. Elsa barks in a high pitch, which gets lower as her impatience grows before, changing to sound like an angry attack dog. Unlike most monsters, Elsa's behavior and physiology is very cartoonish. For example, while Elsa is roaming she is seen to skip, and her tail is shown to spin rapidly like a propeller (which actually allows Elsa to fly).

This "cartoon logic" is best shown when enraged, as Elsa rapidly changes her form, making squishy sounds as she inflates. Elsa's limbs will quickly swell up in size, (starting with the front paws and ending in the back) which leads to her turning into a huge, humanoid creature, with extremely exaggerated muscular features. All dog features are removed with the exception of Elsa's head which remains unchanged and comedically smaller than the rest of her body.

Elsa will roam around aimlessly until spotting a semibot. Upon spotting, it will begin to follow them, occasionally barking, jumping, and staying within their FOV. Elsa can be petted by grabbing it, indicated by heart particles appearing. After receiving five pets, Elsa will be satisfied and walk away while ignoring other semibots temporarily.
If Elsa is thrown into a pit while being conscious, it will fly up using its tail as a propeller.

The longer Elsa goes without being pet while still targeting a semibot, the more frequent its barking and jumping becomes and the redder its eyes become. If Elsa is not pet within roughly 15 seconds or is hurt by any means, it will become enraged, growing into a hulking mass and rushing down the target, dealing contact damage on anything it hits, including the target.
If the targeted semibot is on a higher elevation or hiding under an object, Elsa will appropriately jump or crouch to continue attacking the semibot.
After a certain amount of time, Elsa will shrink back down and return to its normal form, walking away like nothing happened.
While the initial hit of Elsa is fairly weak, it is easy for it to repeatedly slam a player against a wall/object and deal major physics damage.

Elsa essentially acts as an opposite of the Apex Predator, and thus shares many properties with it:
You can use the Duck Bucket on Elsa.
Elsa will quickly lose interest of the semibot it is following if line of sight is broken. If this is done before Elsa gets enraged, it will return to roaming the level.
Once enraged, Elsa will always know where its target is, until it returns to its initial phase.
Be cautious of when Elsa is around other monsters; if hurt by a monster when a player is close, it will enrage regardless and target the closest one.
Elsa can easily be picked up to slam around once stunned. However, due to its extremely high health pool of 600, caution is advised for players attempting this.
You can use an extract to kill Elsa, similar to how the Apex Predator can be killed using the extract.
Once stunned, Elsa will return to its original form. Once the stun is over, Elsa will either turn back to its enraged transformation if a player is close, or stay in its normal form and walk away if no players are around.

It’s possible to hold the grab button while aiming at Elsa to automatically pet it.
Elsa has a lengthy transformation sequence when enraged, players can take advantage of this by making as much distance between them and Elsa as possible, or prepare to setup and retaliate optionally.

Elsa will accept pets from any semibot to satisfy its requirement, even if its not targeting the one who pets it. This is helpful if the target semibot is preoccupied with another task, such as carrying a heavy item.
It takes 5 pets for Elsa to be satisfied.

While it's possible to kill Elsa with enough power or use of a pit, the low value of its orb combined with the robust health pool of 600 and hazard of stunlocking semibots who provoke it, makes Elsa a rather impractical target to deliberately attempt to kill. Not to mention dismissing it peacefully is very easy compared to dismissing it violently. As such, it's better to conserve one's equipment, ammo, and health for other enemies in normal gameplay.

Putting a conscious Elsa into a pit underneath an object, such as the vents in McJannek or the boards in Headman Manor, can cause it to become stuck and exhaust Elsa to death. This leads to easy orb retrieval.
Similar to the Apex Predator, you can force Elsa into fireplaces.
A tranquilized Elsa will revert to normal mode Elsa once unstunned.

There is also a tip that can appear in-game for petting Elsa showing a clip of that same dog.

Elsa shows similarities with the Maneater from Lethal Company, being both small white cute creatures, that demand constant care, or else they become a monster.
Whether this is intentional or not is unclear.

name: Tick
title: Tick
sections: The Tick is a Level 1 monster in R.E.P.O. and was added in V0.3.0 (The Monster update). It acts as a life-draining creature that will steal health from semibots.
1 Appearance
8 References

The Tick is flat beige monster, loosely resembling real-life ticks in its appearance. Its body appears to be a deflated human head. While deflated, it has thick salmon lips that are slightly parted, and two nostrils that resemble black dot eyes. Its real eyes are closed on the sides of the face. Underneath its body are four brown and black insect-like legs that is uses to crawl around. When full after draining health, the Tick's head-like appearance becomes more noticeable.

When draining health from a semibot the tick will expand, its face wincing, and its body blowing up like a balloon and turning from red to green the more health it drains from a semibot. Once full, it's body resembles that of a fat baby's face, with a distinct green glow emanating from inside of it.
The Tick will roam around aimlessly and is initially docile, meaning it will ignore semibots unless provoked.

If the Tick sees a semibot using their grabber, it will emit a warning sound before lunging in the semibot's direction, attempting to latch onto their grabber. If a semibot tries to grab the Tick directly, it will also latch onto their grabber instantly.

Once the Tick is affixed to the grabber, the semibot will be unable to let go, and the Tick will start draining the semibot's health, dealing 10 damage and healing the Tick for 10 HP per second while the Tick is on their grabber. The tick will remain attached to the semibot's grabber until its own health reaches 100. If the tick is damaged during the draining process, it will drain additional health to make up for the loss until it reaches its target threshold. This means that a tick will remain attached to a semibot's grabber until either the semibot dies, the tick dies, or the semibot submits and allows the tick to drain enough health to reach its target of 100 HP.

While stunned, the Tick is still able to attach to the grabber if a semibot attempts to grab it. However, the Tick will immediately detach from the grabber without doing any damage to the semibot. This does not impact the duration of the stun.

Once the Tick reaches 100 HP, it will detach from the grabber and become docile again, trying to flee from semibots; it will not attempt to latch onto grabbers again once it reaches this state even when damaged.

If the Tick is killed without any health drained, it will not drop anything. If killed after draining health it will drop a green pollen-like aura, which will heal any semibots inside it. The amount of health given from the healing aura depends on how much health the Tick drained, although it dissipates rather quickly. If killed when its completely full, it will additionally drop a small Enemy Valuable alongside the healing aura.

If multiple ticks are drawn to the same tractor beam, they will repeatedly interrupt each other in the tractor beam. One will attach, then the other will jump to intercept the tractor beam, causing the first one to drop out of it. Then it in turn will intercept the second one, and this will repeat until they are all satisfied or killed, becoming highly dangerous to a lone semibot due to the constant inability to use their tractor beam whatsoever, as well as the heavy potential health drainage that can occur.

Players attempting to stun or hurt the Tick with a weapon can more difficult for them than one would think, as it will see players holding the weapon and try to lunge at the grabber. This is in addition to the Ticks lunging speed and small size.
Players can get intentionally grabbed by the Tick, then start slamming it, but they must be quick to kill it.
If a player has at least 5 HP to spare, they can tumble into an deflated Tick, which due to its very low hp, will instantly kill it.

Players can deal multiple hits to the Tick by tumbling into it while it's attached, though this is unreliable.

Players should refrain from grabbing anything if they know a Tick is nearby. It can appear anywhere, waiting for the opportunity to intercept their grabber.
Players should remember that grabbing an object that isn't a valuable (ie: door) will still alert the Tick as the Tick is attracted to the grabber.
If players know there is at least one Tick present and they haven't or don't think it has been killed, they should look all around before trying to grab anything as preventative countermeasures are very powerful.

The Tick drains health until its own amount reaches 100, so a normal Tick that starts at 10 HP will drain 90; If you have more than 90 HP but lack any means of stopping power or slamming power to out-damage the tick's leeching ability, consider just letting it drain you until it reaches 100 HP. Once this happens, it becomes docile, and can be picked up and slammed without further consequences. You can reclaim your HP from it after it dies as well as an Orb.
An alternate way of allowing the tick to reach this docile state more easily is to have another semibot healing the one that the Tick is attached to, ensuring their survivability until the Tick drains enough to satisfy itself. The important thing is to not panic if it latches onto you while you have other semibots close by to help.

In spite of its very weak damage output, players can use the Boltzap to one-shot an un-inflated Tick, making it an effective counter against the Tick, as long as a player shoots it before it spots them and lunges towards their grabber.

The health aura heals all semibots inside it even though it only drains from one; this can be used to essentially gain free HP, by letting it drain a semibot and then killing it to heal multiple semibots, which will give the drained semibot their HP back, as well as healing other semibots for free (along with providing a free Orb).
Players can use their body to block the tick from latching onto nearby players letting the nearby semibot leave the room with the valuable and not be afraid of the tick latching on.

The Tick's suck frequency now slows as it grows. Detaches when far enough from its attached player.
According to the dev logs, the Tick would be about the size of a football in the real world.[2]
The Tick may be a reference to the fat-sucking creatures that appear in The Ozempic Problem by MeatCanyon. Both are bug like creatures with a big head for a body, and suck the life out of a target.

The Gambit is a level 2 monster in R.E.P.O. and was added in V0.3.0 (The Monster Update). It acts as a purely luck-based monster that can either help or harm the semibots.
1 Appearance

6 History

6.1 V0.3.0
6.2 V0.3.1.2 beta

The Gambit appears as a medium-sized humanoid entity with a small body. The Gambits head is comically large, on its face, it has some small, sunken, black eyes, it has a tongue in the middle of its face, constantly sticking out, On its lower body, it has long arms small legs and feet, and a small butt a the rear end.
When the Gambits mouth is opened, inside of it is revealed to be a huge, multi-colored roulette wheel. The Gambit is also revealed to have some sparse and crooked teeth around the roulette wheel.
While gambling, running, or upon death, the Gambit’s Wheel plays a circus-like tune, although the tune is muffled if its mouth is closed. To hear it, see audio below.
On the Gambit's wheel are some colored spaces. The 5 different colors on the wheel are as follows:
Additionally, the Gambit's tongue is used as the hand that picks the chosen space.

The Gambit will roam around aimlessly, but when it spots a semibot, the Gambit will give chase until it grabs or loses them. Note that Gambits aware of a semibot have no pause before attempting to grab a semibot under any object.

If the Gambit is successful in grabbing the targeted semibot, it will hold them in tumble mode immediately in front of it. The Gambit will then open its mouth, which reveals the large roulette wheel within. The wheel will spin, with the targeted semibot forced to watch until it lands on one of the wheel's colors.
There are 9 Colored spaces in total, and whatever color is landed on determines the reward for the grabbed semibot. The corresponding colors and rewards are shown below:
The Gambit plays a losing buzzer sound and the grabbed semibot is shocked with red electricity.
The Gambit plays a brief calming note and the grabbed semibot is pampered with health particles.
The Gambit plays a winning buzzer sound and gifts the semibot one Money bag to extract.
The Gambit plays an angelic jingle and the grabbed semibot is blessed with white healing particles.
The Gambit plays a dramatic stinger and the grabbed semibot is zapped with black electricity. (This sound is heard throughout the map, regardless of who got it.)

If a Gambit is stunned in any way while the wheel is currently spinning or it is giving the reward, it will be interrupted and produce an explosion which deals 60 damage to the held semibot, as well as canceling the reward from the spin if not already given.

After a Gambit has given the reward to the grabbed semibot, it will close its mouth - hiding the wheel, drop the held semibot if they survived, and run away. During this phase, it will not target or chase any semibots and will sprint to a random, far away area. Afterwards, Gambit will resume its roaming behavior.

As Gambit has positive rewards, players are not entirely discouraged from being grabbed by it.
However, as there is a 50% chance of landing on a red space and 6.25% chance of landing on a black space, there is a 56.25% chance of a negative reward.
Additionally, if the player only desires health as a reward, green (25%) and white (6.25%) only make up a 31.25% chance of occurring.

Semibots are not invulnerable to other attacks while held by a Gambit, making their grab additionally dangerous in tandem with other nearby monsters.
There is a very brief moment between a player being grabbed and the Gambit actually starting its spinning wheel animation where stunning it will not cause any explosion for interrupting.

Players are able to attack the Gambit during the roulette wheel to potentially interrupt it. However, if they do this during the spinning, the interruption explosion will still occur, dealing 60 damage. Despite this, it may be worth it if Gambit was about to land black, as the explosion would deal a fixed amount rather than setting the semibot's health to 1.

If grabbed, a semibot can grab Gambit rapidly to force it to instantly begin spinning - skipping the initial delay before the spin starts.
Keep in mind that if the semibot has Strength of 9 or more, holding for too long while grabbing will mean that they lifted the Gambit, which counts as a stun and thus results in the interruption explosion penalty.
